profile: The teen with a first paycheck
title: The $200 Shoes Decision
scenario: A teenager wants new sneakers but also needs money for transportation, a phone contribution, and savings.
steps: Start with a fictional $250 paycheck.
List the expenses that must be covered before the next paycheck.
See what remains after buying the shoes.
Compare buying now, choosing a cheaper pair, or saving toward them.
goal: Understand spending tradeoffs and needs versus wants.

title: More Than the Rent
scenario: A young adult is preparing to move into their first apartment and has only considered rent.
steps: Review fictional take-home income.
Add utilities, groceries, transportation, and internet.
Separate move-in costs from recurring monthly expenses.
Compare two housing options using the complete budget.
goal: Recognize the full cost of living independently.

profile: The hourly worker with changing hours
title: When the Paycheck Shrinks
scenario: An hourly worker receives less pay than expected while regular expenses remain.
steps: Compare the expected and actual fictional paycheck.
Identify essential expenses and upcoming due dates.
Adjust flexible spending.
Spot any remaining shortfall and identify questions to ask the bill provider.
goal: Practice budgeting with income that changes.

title: The School Expense Surprise
scenario: A parent, including a single-parent household, faces a school expense alongside groceries and household bills.
steps: Add the fictional school expense to the monthly plan.
Separate required costs from optional extras.
Compare ways to adjust flexible expenses.
Create a small future school-expense savings goal.
goal: Plan for irregular family costs without losing sight of essentials.

profile: The adult juggling debt and daily costs
title: The Trip and the Oil Change
scenario: An adult has budgeted for a getaway but overlooked routine car maintenance and existing payment obligations.
steps: Add maintenance to the fictional trip budget.
Review household bills and required debt payments.
Compare a smaller trip, a later trip, and the original plan.
See how each choice changes the money remaining.
goal: Include overlooked costs and compare spending priorities.

title: A Different Monthly Income
scenario: A worker explores a fictional future budget with less monthly income.
steps: Compare two fictional monthly income amounts.
List essential expenses.
Review subscriptions and flexible spending.
Identify costs and income details that still need verification.
goal: Understand how an income change affects a household budget.

profile: The new retiree on a monthly payment
title: Make It Last Until Next Month
scenario: A new retiree receives income once a month and needs to plan around bills, groceries, and transportation.
steps: Place fictional income and bill dates on a calendar.
Reserve money for bills due later in the month.
Divide flexible spending into weekly amounts.
Check what remains before the next payment.
goal: Understand payment timing and monthly cash flow.

profile: The older adult balancing medicine and lottery spending
title: Medicine Before the Maybe
scenario: A 70-year-old on a fixed income discovers that repeated lottery purchases have used money needed for a prescription refill.
steps: Review a fictional monthly income and prescription cost.
Add up the month’s lottery purchases.
Build a budget that reserves money for medicine and other essentials first.
Compare smaller entertainment amounts and see their effect.
If the fictional budget still falls short, identify who to contact about prescription costs, such as a pharmacist or insurer.
goal: Recognize repeated discretionary spending and protect essential expenses.
